study_identification_part.si_4_title: Lifespan development of thalamic nuclei and characterizing thalamic nuclei abnormalities in schizophrenia using normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: HCP-D (Human Connectome Project Development, ages 5-21); HCP-YA (Human Connectome Project Young Adult/S1200, ages 21-35); HCP-A (Human Connectome Project Aging, ages 36-100+); SINGLE-SITE (Schizophrenia Cohort collected at Vanderbilt University Medical Center)
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Normative modeling of thalamic nuclei development was conducted using data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) Lifespan Studies (combined n = 2490). The HCP Lifespan studies include three independent large-scale, publicly available population-based samples of typically developing individuals covering the human lifespan from ages 5-100+: the original HCP S1200 sample (ages 21-35, n = 1113); HCP Development Lifespan (2.0 release, ages 5-21, n = 652); and HCP Aging Lifespan (2.0 release, ages 36-100+, n = 725)." ... "Individual deviations in thalamus volumes were drawn from a repository study comprising 643 individuals who participated in one of three neuroimaging projects"

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: HCP Lifespan datasets (HCP-D, HCP-YA, HCP-A) were combined to construct normative models of thalamic nuclei development across the lifespan (ages 5-100+). The Schizophrenia Cohort (SINGLE-SITE) was used as an independent clinical sample to apply the normative models and determine frequency of thalamic volume deviations in people with schizophrenia.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative modeling of thalamic nuclei development was conducted using data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) Lifespan Studies" ... "we characterized the development of thalamic nuclei volumes using normative models generated from the Human Connectome Project Lifespan datasets (5-100+ years), then applied them to an independent clinical cohort to determine the frequency of thalamic volume deviations in people with schizophrenia"

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was constructed using GAMLSS (Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape) for thalamic nuclei volumes across the lifespan. The final sample after exclusions was 1952 (HCP S1200 n=825, Development HCP n=525, Aging HCP n=602). The paper does not distinguish between train and test phases - all data appears to have been used for model fitting. Additionally, 211 healthy controls from the Schizophrenia Cohort were used to validate model generalization.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "After randomly removing twins to avoid biasing the normative lifespan model and excluding individuals with poor quality scans or segmentation failures, the final sample was 1952 (HCP S1200 n = 825, Development HCP n = 525, Aging HCP n = 725)." Note: Supplementary Table 1 shows Aging N=602, Overall N=1952.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics for the combined HCP Lifespan Cohort (N=1952) used for normative modeling. Subsamples: Development (N=525): mean 14.8 (SD 3.97), median 14.6, range 5.60-21.9 years; Young Adult (N=825): mean 28.7 (SD 3.76), median 29.0, range 22.0-37.0 years; Aging (N=602): mean 59.6 (SD 15.4), median 57.6, range 36.0-100 years. No separate train/test split was reported; all data was used for model fitting.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex distribution for the combined HCP Lifespan Cohort (N=1952) used for normative modeling. Subsamples: Development (N=525): Female 276 (53%), Male 249 (47%); Young Adult (N=825): Female 449 (54%), Male 376 (46%); Aging (N=602): Female 346 (57%), Male 256 (43%). No separate train/test split was reported.
